newsitem.title: JAPAN: HSBC Group to construct own building in Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: HSBC Group to construct own building in Tokyo.

text.p: The HSBC Group, headed by flagship company Hongkong and Shanghai Banking Corp., is planning to construct its own building in Tokyo's business district, a Hongkong Bank spokeswoman said on Monday.

The planned 10-storey building, which will house the five Tokyo HSBC companies, among them Midland Bank Plc and HSBC Securities, is seen by the group as emphasising its continuing presence in Japan, public affairs manager Mariko Terazaki told Reuters.
"We hope the building reflects our commitment to Japan," she said.
Terazaki added that this was not a shift in the group's emphasis on its operations from other Asian centres, but merely a buildup of its strength in Japan.

"Hong Kong and Singapore are very good markets, very exciting and in some ways more open, but Tokyo is the largest in Asia. (Its) economy will probably pick up soon and we want to be ready to take part when this happens," she said.

She also said that while a total 12 people had been hired this year by Midland Bank and HSBC Securities, this was due partly to natural attrition and there was no plan in place now for a substantial increase in overall staffing.

Some foreign banks have recently said they will increase their presence in Japan. French bank Societe Generale SGOP.PA said in July it was expanding its foreign exchange operations in Tokyo, partly as a result of the yen's depreciation against the dollar.
While Terazaki said the weaker yen was certainly welcome, it had not had a significant impact on the group's plans.
Construction is set to begin this month and end in April 1998.
